stable_examples_to_add.title: Paper two-input operator CMs
stable_examples_to_add.purpose: Derive the sixteen two-input Boolean functions and show their complete 2x2 matrices under the paper's state order.
stable_examples_to_add.definition: Rows are X and not-X; columns are Y and not-Y. AND=[[1,0],[0,0]], OR=[[1,1],[1,0]], XOR=[[0,1],[1,0]], equivalence=[[1,0],[0,1]], implication=[[1,0],[1,1]].

stable_examples_to_add.title: Paper LM-to-4x4-CM construction
stable_examples_to_add.purpose: Distinguish expression-valued LMs from binary CMs and trace one paper construction through positive valuation.
stable_examples_to_add.definition: The paper's worked expression (W XOR X) implies (not Y AND Z), measured with left state Y,W and right state X,Z, yields valued rows 1100,1110,0011,1011.

episodes_to_add.title: Why there are sixteen 2x2 operator CMs
episodes_to_add.thesis: Two Boolean inputs have four ordered assignments; choosing one output for each defines a complete binary Boolean function, so there are exactly sixteen functions represented in the paper by sixteen distinct 2x2 operator CMs.
owns: four state pairs for a binary Boolean function
paper state ordering for operator CMs
excludes: No logical-matrix derivation, repository rectangular layout, CM-IR, packed-output, solver, or benchmark mechanism is taught here.
teaching_beats: Ask sixteen what, then distinguish sixteen functions from sixteen assignments.
Move the four input pairs into the paper's X/not-X by Y/not-Y state order.
Populate AND and distinguish one entry from one complete operator matrix.
Derive 2^4=16 from four independent binary output choices.
Read named examples in the full Figure 1 gallery without demanding memorization.
Swap operands for implication to demonstrate ordering dependence.
Retrieve XOR from its unlabeled output pattern.
Handoff from binary entries to expression-valued logical matrices.
visual_spine: Four persistent assignment cards move from truth-table order into the paper's 2x2 state order.
One complete operator matrix expands into sixteen complete 2x2 patterns through four binary choices.
Named symmetric and asymmetric operators illuminate inside the Figure 1 gallery.
An unlabeled XOR matrix supports retrieval before the name appears.

dialogue_anchors.hook: There are sixteen matrices here, but sixteen what?
dialogue_anchors.definition: One complete 2x2 binary pattern represents one complete two-input Boolean function under a declared state order.
dialogue_anchors.boundary: These are not sixteen assignments of one four-variable function and they are not repository layouts.
dialogue_anchors.closing: One cell is one state-pair output; one complete matrix is one operator.

episodes_to_add.retrieval_check: Read the four ordered outputs of the unlabeled XOR matrix before naming the operator.
episodes_to_add.closing_takeaway: Four ordered input cases allow sixteen complete output patterns and therefore sixteen two-input operator CMs.
misconceptions: The sixteen matrices are sixteen assignments or sixteen cells of one larger function.
One positive matrix cell is itself the logical operator.
caveats: The state/operand order must remain visible, especially for asymmetric operators.

episodes_to_add.title: From logical matrices to higher-dimensional CMs
episodes_to_add.thesis: The paper's logical matrices contain logical expressions, positive valuation produces their binary CMs, and projection/tensor/modifier structure extends the construction to larger square matrices for compound logic.
excludes: No repository rectangular materialization, CM-IR implementation, or benchmark result is taught here.
teaching_beats: Replace binary CM entries with expression-valued LM entries.
Construct the base two-variable LM in the paper's state order.
Apply positive valuation entrywise and recover a binary operator CM.
Project/tensor smaller logical matrices into a 4x4 expression-valued structure.
Substitute the paper's worked compound expression and apply the implication modifier.
Reveal the exact valued 4x4 CM and its Y,W by X,Z order.
Retrieve the LM-versus-CM classification from one persistent cell.
State the paper's square higher-dimensional rule and separate it from repository rectangles.
visual_spine: One persistent matrix cell changes type only through visible positive valuation.
A process rail grows 2x2 LM to tensor/projection to 4x4 LM to valued CM.
The paper's compound expression feeds an implication modifier and settles into an exact 4x4 binary matrix.
Square paper growth and rectangular repository preview remain on separated rails.

dialogue_anchors.hook: What does a matrix look like before its entries have become bits?
dialogue_anchors.definition: An LM contains logical expressions; the paper's positive valuation produces the corresponding binary CM.
dialogue_anchors.boundary: The paper's formal higher-dimensional construction is square and is not the repository's arbitrary rectangular API rule.
dialogue_anchors.closing: Expressions first, valuation second, binary CM afterward.

episodes_to_add.retrieval_check: Classify one persistent entry before and after positive valuation as belonging to an LM or a CM.
episodes_to_add.closing_takeaway: The paper builds larger logical matrices for compound logic and obtains their CMs through positive valuation.
misconceptions: An LM and CM are two names for the same binary array.
The paper creates its 4x4 example by arbitrarily reshaping a truth column.
caveats: Bra-ket notation remains secondary to the visible state and valuation actions.
The paper is an author manuscript; its framework claims are not upgraded to peer-reviewed consensus.
